source_text: ἐν ὑπερηφανίᾳ ὥστε μὴ ὑπακοῦσαι τοῦ ἱερέως τοῦ παρεστηκότος λειτουργεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ σου, ἢ τοῦ κριτοῦ ὃς ἂν ᾖ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις, καὶ ἀποθανεῖται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος, καὶ ἐξαρεῖς τὸν πονηρὸν ἐξ Ἰσραήλ. Καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας φοβηθήσεται, καὶ οὐκ ἀσεβήσει ἔτι.» Ὁρᾷς ἐπισκήπτοντα σαφῶς τὸν νόμον τοῖς κατὰ πᾶσαν αἰτίαν ἐγκαλεῖν ᾑρημένοις, κριτήν τε καὶ διαγνώμονα ποιεῖσθαι τὸν ἱερουργόν. Ἀλλὰ φυλάξῃ σφόδρα ποιῆσαι κατὰ πάντα ὅσα ἂν νομοθετηθῇ σοι. «Χείλη γὰρ ἱερέως φυλάξεται κρίσιν, καὶ νόμον ζητήσουσιν ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ,» κατὰ τὴν τοῦ προφήτου φωνήν. Νομοθετεῖ μὲν γὰρ ἥκιστα μὲν αὐτὸς, ἀποκομίζει δὲ μᾶλλον εἰς τὸ εὐθὺ τὸ τῷ νομοθέτῃ δοκοῦν ἀδεκάστως ἀφηγούμενος, καὶ δικαιοσύνης ὑπάρχων ἄριστος βραβευτὴς, τὴν ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ κρίσιν ταλαντεύει λεπτῶς. Ἀγριότητος δὲ καὶ ὑπεροψίας ταύτῃτοι γραφὴ τοῖς ἀπειθεῖν ἑλομένοις ἀκολουθεῖ, καὶ τὸ παντῶν ἐπέκεινα διεληλακὸς τῶν κακῶν, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ὁ θάνατος καθορίζεται, Τεθνήξεται γὰρ ὃς ἂν ἀλογήσῃ, φησὶ, τοῦ ἱερέως τοῦ παρεστηκότος λειτουργεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ. Μέγα δὴ οὖν καὶ οὐκ ἀθαύμαστον ἀληθῶς, ἡ ὑπὸ Θεῷ παράστασίς τε καὶ λειτουργία. Ὁ δὲ τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ λειτουργὸν ἀτιμάσας, ὑπὸ δίκην ἔσται καὶ κόλασιν, καὶ ὁ τὸ θεῖον ἀξίωμα περιπτύων, πικροὺς τῆς ὑπεροψίας ἀποτίσει λόγους. Πεφροντικότα δὲ καὶ αὐτὸν εὑρήσομεν τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τῆς εἰς τόνδε τὸν νόμον αἰδοῦς. Προσεφώνει γὰρ ὡδὶ τοῖς Ἰουδαίων λαοῖς· «Ἐπὶ τῆς Μωσέως καθέδρας ἐκάθισαν οἱ Γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι· πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἂν λέγωσιν ὑμῖν, ποιεῖτε, κατὰ δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν μὴ ποιεῖτε.» Μηδεὶς οὖν κρινέτω τὸν ἱερουργὸν, κἂν εἰ παρειμένος ὁρῷτό πως, καὶ εἰ τὸ ῥᾴθυμον ἔχοι πρός γε τὸ βιοῦν ἑλέσθαι συννόμως, διερμηνεύοντι δὲ τὸν νόμον, προσκομιζέτω τὴν εὐπείθειαν. Πάσχει μὲν γὰρ τὰ ἀπὸ γνώμης οἰκείας, ἐξηγεῖται δὲ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ. Οὐκ ἀτιμαστέον οὖν τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ διὰ τὰ ἀνθρώπινα. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οὐ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Λαμπρὸν δὲ ὅτι καὶ ἀπόβλεπτον ἀληθῶς τῆς ἱερωσύνης τὸ χρῆμα, κἀντεῦθεν εἴσῃ τοι· ἐπισημοτάτην μὲν γὰρ ἔχει τὴν εἰσβολὴν, καὶ μέν τοι καὶ τὴν κατάληξιν. Οὐδὲ γὰρ ἄν τις λάθοι πρὸς ἱερουργίαν ἠγμένος, ἤγουν κεκλημένος παρὰ Θεοῦ, πρὸς τὰς ἄνω τε καὶ ἐν οὐρανῷ μονὰς, καὶ μεθεὶς ἑτέρῳ τὴν ἱερωσύνην. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς, τοὺς τὸ εὐαγγελικὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἱερουργοῦντας κήρυγμα, καὶ προσέτι τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ πάντη τε καὶ πάντως ἔσεσθαι περιφανεῖς, καὶ ἀπόβλεπτον ἔφη λαχεῖν τὴν δόξαν. «Οὐδεὶς γὰρ λύχνον ἅψας, εἰς τὸ κρυπτὸν τίθησιν, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ὑπὸ κλίνην,» φησὶν, «ἤγουν ὑπὸ μόδιον, ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, ἵνα πάντες οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι, τὸ φῶς βλέπωσιν·» ἀληθὲς γὰρ ὅτι εἰρημένον, τὸ ἐν δόξῃ φημὶ τῇ περιφανεῖ καὶ τεθαυμασμένῃ, τὸν θεῖον ἔσεσθαι λειτουργὸν, ἀναπειθέτω βοῶν καὶ
pass_a_gloss: [Deut 17:12b–13 LXX:] …in arrogance so as not to obey the priest standing by to minister in the name of the Lord your God, or the judge who is in those days, and that man will die, and you will remove the evil one from Israel; and all the people hearing will fear and no longer act impiously. || You see the law clearly enjoining those who have chosen to accuse/complain on every cause to make the priest officiant judge and arbiter. But you will keep very much to do according to all that is legislated for you. For 'lips of a priest will guard judgment, and law they will seek from his mouth', according to the prophet's voice. For he legislates least of all himself, but rather carries back straight what seems good to the lawgiver, narrating impartially, and being best umpire of justice, weighs finely the judgment on each. An indictment of savagery and contempt for this reason follows those choosing to disobey, and the thing that has passed beyond all evils, that is, death, is determined; for he will die who disregards, it says, the priest standing by to minister in the name of the Lord God. || Great then and not unwondrous truly the standing by under God and ministry. The one dishonoring the minister of God will be under penalty and punishment, and the one spitting upon the divine dignity will pay bitter accounts of contempt. We will find our Lord Jesus Christ himself having cared for the reverence toward this law; for he addressed the peoples of the Jews: 'on Moses' seat sat the scribes and Pharisees; all then whatever they tell you, do; but according to their works do not do.' Let no one then judge the priest officiant, even if seen somehow slack, and if he has laziness toward choosing to live lawfully; but to him interpreting the law let him bring compliance. For he suffers the things from his own judgment, but expounds the things of God. Not to be dishonored then the things of God because of the human. || PALL.: Not indeed. || CYR.: That bright and truly looked at is the thing of priesthood, you will know from here too: it has a most notable entry and indeed the ending. For no one would escape notice being led to priestly ministry, or called by God to the mansions above and in heaven, and having let go the priesthood to another. Therefore Christ too said those performing priestly service the gospel proclamation to the nations, and besides to those of Israel, would be in every way and altogether conspicuous, and obtain a looked at glory. 'For no one having lit a lamp puts it in the hidden place, nor under a bed', he says, 'or under a bushel, but on the lampstand, that all those coming in may see the light.' That it has been said truly — I mean that the divine minister will be in glory conspicuous and admired — let persuade, crying out, also…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …in arrogance, so as not to obey the priest who stands to minister in the name of the Lord your God, or the judge who is in office in those days, that man shall die, and you shall remove the wicked person from Israel. And all the people, when they hear, will be afraid, and will no longer act impiously.’ (Deuteronomy 17:8–13) You see how the law clearly charges those who have chosen to bring a complaint on any ground to make the priest their judge and arbiter. Indeed, ‘you shall take great care to act in keeping with all that is laid down for you’ (Deuteronomy 17:10). For ‘the lips of a priest will guard judgment, and they will seek the law from his mouth,’ as the prophet says (Malachi 2:7). He does not make law himself at all; rather, he conveys faithfully what the lawgiver has decided, setting it out without partiality, and, as the best arbiter of justice, he weighs the judgment in each case with precision. For this reason a charge of savagery and contempt follows those who choose to disobey, and the worst of all evils, that is, death, is appointed for them. For whoever disregards the priest who stands to minister in the name of the Lord God, it says, shall die (Deuteronomy 17:12). Great, then, and truly wonderful is this attendance and ministry under God. Whoever dishonors God’s minister will be subject to judgment and punishment, and whoever spurns the divine dignity will render a bitter account for his contempt. We shall find that our Lord Jesus Christ himself was also concerned for the respect due to this law. For he addressed the crowds of the Jews in this way: ‘The scribes and the Pharisees have sat on Moses’ seat; so do all that they tell you, but do not do as they do.’ (Matthew 23:2–3) So let no one judge the priest, even if he is seen to be somewhat slack, and even if he is careless about choosing to live in keeping with the law; but when he interprets the law, let everyone give him ready obedience. For his weaknesses arise from his own will, but what he expounds belongs to God. The things of God, then, must not be dishonored because of what is human.

Cyril: You will learn from this too that the priesthood is a splendid thing, and truly one on which all eyes are fixed. Its beginning is most conspicuous, and so too is its close. For no one could pass unnoticed when he is brought to priestly service, nor again when he is called by God to the dwellings above in heaven and hands the priesthood on to another. That is why Christ too said that those who serve as priests in proclaiming the gospel to the nations (Romans 15:16), and to those of Israel besides, would be conspicuous in every way and without fail, and would receive a glory on which all eyes are fixed. ‘For no one, after lighting a lamp, puts it in a hidden place, nor even under a bed,’ he says, ‘or under a basket, but on the lampstand, so that all who come in may see the light.’ (Luke 11:33; Luke 8:16) That this was truly said, I mean that the divine minister will be in a glory that is conspicuous and admired, let the inspired Isaiah also convince you, when he cries out:

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 13 to compare. Sense taken from the PG 68 Greek. The withheld earlier English was not used as a model.

apparatus.note: Section opens mid-quotation (Deuteronomy 17:12, begun at the end of section 20) and mid-turn; the quotation closes after 17:13. 'You shall remove the evil one': τὸν πονηρόν may be 'the evil one' or 'the evil', kept personal as the context is the man put to death. 'But you shall take great care to do…' (φυλάξῃ σφόδρα ποιῆσαι κατὰ πάντα ὅσα ἂν νομοθετηθῇ σοι) is Cyril's re-quotation of Deuteronomy 17:10 LXX (which has φυλάξῃ σφόδρα ποιῆσαι); set as a quotation and cited. Malachi 2:7 LXX reads χείλη ἱερέως φυλάξεται γνῶσιν ('knowledge'); Cyril's text has κρίσιν ('judgment'), which suits his argument about the priest as judge; translated as he quotes it. 'For whoever disregards the priest… shall die' is a paraphrase of Deuteronomy 17:12, cited without quotation marks. ἀποκομίζει εἰς τὸ εὐθύ rendered 'conveys faithfully' ('carries back straight'). γραφή taken in its legal sense, 'a charge' (indictment). 'The standing in service under God' renders ἡ ὑπὸ Θεῷ παράστασις. πάσχει τὰ ἀπὸ γνώμης οἰκείας ('he suffers the things from his own will') rendered 'what he undergoes comes from his own will': Cyril means the priest's private failings are his own affair, while his teaching is God's. In 'nor again when he is called by God to the dwellings above', ἤγουν (usually 'that is') must here mark the second member (the 'close') against the first (the 'entry'), so it is rendered 'nor again'; μοναί may echo John 14:2 but the allusion is faint and left uncited. 'Those who serve as priests in proclaiming the gospel to the nations' (τὸ εὐαγγελικὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἱερουργοῦντας κήρυγμα) is a clear verbal echo of Romans 15:16 (ἱερουργοῦντα τὸ εὐαγγέλιον… εἰς τὰ ἔθνη) and is cited. The lamp saying conflates Luke 11:33 (εἰς κρύπτην… οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον… ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι… βλέπωσιν) and Luke 8:16 (ὑποκάτω κλίνης… βλέπωσιν τὸ φῶς); ἤγουν ὑπὸ μόδιον ('or rather under a bushel') stands inside the quotation, rendered 'or under a basket'. Matthew 5:15 is close but lacks the 'bed' and 'those who come in'. The section ends mid-sentence (ἀναπειθέτω βοῶν καὶ | ὁ θεσπέσιος Ἡσαΐας); following the old row split, Isaiah's name is placed here and the quotation (Isaiah 40:9) opens section 22. Review: ἀλλὰ φυλάξῃ σφόδρα… — ἀλλά is Cyril's connective, not part of Deuteronomy 17:10 LXX, so it stands outside the quotation as 'Indeed'. τὸν πονηρόν rendered 'the wicked person' (not 'the evil one', which English readers hear as Satan). πάσχει μὲν γὰρ τὰ ἀπὸ γνώμης οἰκείας rendered 'his weaknesses arise from his own will': πάσχει here refers back to the slackness (παρειμένος, τὸ ῥᾴθυμον) just named, so the sense is his own failings; a more literal 'what he undergoes' was unclear. τῇ περιφανεῖ καὶ τεθαυμασμένῃ agrees with δόξῃ, so 'a glory that is conspicuous and admired'.

'the standing in service under God and the ministry' (calque) -> 'this attendance and ministry under God'
'spits on… pay a bitter reckoning' -> 'spurns… render a bitter account'
'took care for reverence toward this law' -> 'was concerned for the respect due to this law'
Matt 23:3: 'do not do according to their works' -> 'do not do as they do'; 'seat of Moses' -> 'Moses’ seat'

Fronted ὅτι-clause on the priesthood put in natural order; εἰσβολή 'entry' -> 'beginning'; 'can' -> 'could' (potential optative)
